Recent proposals of superwind mass-loss with an L/M dependence contrast with traditional L-only RSG wind recipes, but their impact on late-time evolution of massive stars is unclear.
AI.method: Stellar evolution models were computed with MESA for initial masses of 10–40 M⊙, comparing the VS23 L/M mass-loss recipe against traditional prescriptions. Predicted emission-line spectra were generated with the PoWR stellar atmosphere code. An analytical model was also developed (Appendix A) to study runaway stripping as a function of inverse mass-loss scaling strength.
AI.result: For a 25 M⊙ star, the L/M recipe yields mass-loss rates an order of magnitude higher than traditional recipes due to the inverse mass dependence. Because RSG luminosity is set by core mass and is largely insensitive to current stellar mass, this produces a positive feedback loop driving runaway envelope stripping. Stars with M_init ~ 20 M⊙ can strip their hydrogen envelope and form classical Wolf-Rayet stars (confirmed by HRD location and PoWR spectra). Stars with M_init < 20 M⊙ do not fully strip and expand after core helium burning.
AI.conclusion: An L/M-dependent RSG mass-loss prescription enables a viable single-star pathway into the yellow supergiant and Wolf-Rayet regimes. The degree of full versus partial stripping directly affects supernova progenitors, including partially stripped type IIb SNe. Runaway stripping increases rapidly with the strength of the inverse mass scaling.

title: Resolving the physics of Quasar Ly$α$ Nebulae (RePhyNe): II. The dense and clumpy CGM of Quasars at $z \sim$ 3.5
comment: 13 pages + 4 appendix pages, 7 + 6 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: The small scale density distribution of the cold circumgalactic medium (CGM) plays a central role in galaxy evolution, yet it is still poorly understood. We provide new constraints on the cold CGM density distribution by comparing the CGM emission from MUSE observations of quasar (QSO) nebulae at $z \sim 3.8$ with mock observations generated from the new DaLya simulation suite under the assumption of maximal fluorescence. These are further complemented by mock observations generated from the COLIBRE (m5 and m6 resolutions) and HELLO simulations. We first investigate the distribution of the observed and simulated Ly$α$ surface brightness (SB) values, which directly depend on the cold gas density distribution under our assumption, finding stark differences between observations and upper limits provided by simulations with the exception of the COLIBRE higher-resolution run (m5). The observations generally show a much larger covering fraction of regions with relatively large Ly$α$ SB values and suggest that densities reaching at least 10 cm$^{-3}$ must be present in the CGM of QSOs within a radial distance of 50 to 200 ckpc. To understand the origin of this discrepancy, we study the cold CGM density distribution finding in all cases simulated PDFs consistent with skewed lognormal ones with medians $\sim 10^{-2}$ cm$^{-3}$ and clumping factors between 16 and 102. We compare the broadness of these distributions to the one implied by the observed HeII/Ly$α$ CGM ratio, which is independent on the assumption of maximum fluorescence. Assuming lognormal PDFs with median values similar to the simulations, the observed ratio requires a broader PDF with a clumping factor at least 8 times larger than predicted by simulations. These results suggest that higher resolution and/or additional physical mechanisms are needed to reproduce the observed CGM of QSOs at these redshifts.

AI.tldr: Comparing MUSE QSO nebula observations at z~3.8 with mock observations from DaLya, COLIBRE, and HELLO simulations, the study finds that simulated cold CGM density distributions are too narrow, requiring clumping factors at least 8 times larger than predicted to match observed Lyα and HeII/Lyα ratios.
AI.motivation: The small-scale density distribution of the cold circumgalactic medium (CGM) is central to galaxy evolution but remains poorly constrained. This work aims to provide new observational constraints on cold CGM density structure at z~3.8.
AI.method: The authors compare Lyα surface brightness (SB) from MUSE observations of QSO nebulae at z~3.8 with mock observations from the DaLya simulation suite under the maximal fluorescence assumption, complemented by COLIBRE (m5, m6) and HELLO simulations. They analyze the SB distribution and the cold CGM density PDF, and compare the PDF broadness to that implied by the observed HeII/Lyα ratio, which is independent of the maximal fluorescence assumption.
AI.result: Observations show a much larger covering fraction of high Lyα SB regions than most simulations, except the COLIBRE m5 run, implying cold gas densities reaching at least 10 cm^-3 within 50–200 ckpc of QSOs. Simulated density PDFs are skewed lognormal with medians ~10^-2 cm^-3 and clumping factors of 16–102. The observed HeII/Lyα ratio requires a clumping factor at least 8 times larger than simulated predictions.
AI.conclusion: Higher resolution and/or additional physical mechanisms are needed to reproduce the observed cold CGM of QSOs at these redshifts, as current simulations underestimate the broadness of the cold gas density distribution.

title: A New Framework for Modeling Solar Flares from MHD to Kinetic Processes
comment: 21 pages, 12 figures, accepted for publication by Astrophysical Journal
summary: Physical processes in solar flares span many orders of magnitude in spatiotemporal scales, so a single unified model accounting for all relevant processes remains computationally intractable. Instead, specialized codes have been developed, targeting specific domains that tackle specific aspects of the solar flare problem. Here, we present a comprehensive framework that links three models to capture flare initiation and energy release, the subsequent particle acceleration, the propagation and thermalization of those particles, and ultimately the heating of the lower solar atmosphere. We use the 2.5D ARMS magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code to model stressing of the magnetic field in a simulated active region, the formation of a current sheet, magnetic reconnection, and the evolution of newly formed flare loops. We use the conditions in the ARMS' current sheet to initialize the kglobal model, which predicts time-dependent nonthermal electron and proton distributions. Finally, we use RADYN+FP to inject these distributions into a newly reconnected ARMS loop and compute subsequent particle transport, atmospheric heating, and radiative emissions. This is the first detailed presentation of a RADYN+FP simulation tracking nonthermal electrons and protons in the same loop. As well as discussing the interesting physics that takes place, we note how this results in white-light flare emission height consistent with observations. This work is a first step toward building a fully 3D flare modeling framework.

AI.tldr: A linked three-code framework (ARMS MHD, kglobal, RADYN+FP) models solar flare initiation, particle acceleration, transport, and lower-atmosphere heating, reproducing observed white-light emission heights.
AI.motivation: Solar flare processes span many orders of magnitude in spatiotemporal scales, making a single unified model computationally intractable. Specialized codes each cover only specific domains, so an integrated framework linking them is needed to capture the full flare chain.
AI.method: Chain three specialized codes: 2.5D ARMS MHD models magnetic field stressing, current sheet formation, reconnection, and flare loop evolution; the ARMS current sheet conditions initialize kglobal, which predicts time-dependent nonthermal electron and proton distributions; these distributions are injected into a newly reconnected ARMS loop via RADYN+FP to compute particle transport, atmospheric heating, and radiative emission.
AI.result: First detailed RADYN+FP simulation tracking nonthermal electrons and protons in the same loop; the framework yields white-light flare emission heights consistent with observations.
AI.conclusion: Linking these three codes captures flare initiation, energy release, particle acceleration, propagation/thermalization, and lower-atmosphere heating, serving as a first step toward a fully 3D flare modeling framework.

title: Constraining the density distribution of the cold Circumgalactic Medium of quasars at z>2 through Lya, HeII and Ha emission
comment: 21 pages, 15 figures, 6 tables in total, including an 8-page appendix with 9 figures and 5 tables. Submitted to A&A on 6 August 2026
summary: Extended Lya emission is routinely detected around high-redshift quasars, revealing large reservoirs of cool circumgalactic medium (CGM). Its resonant nature complicates interpretation of gas density, ionization state, and kinematics, making non-resonant tracers such as HeII and Ha essential. Extending previous analytical models, we use CLOUDY photo-ionization simulations to predict HeII/Ha in quasar-illuminated gas over a broad parameter range, including log-normal density distributions. The ratio constrains density fluctuations, commonly quantified by the clumping factor C. We compare the models with extended Lya, HeII, and Ha observations around quasars at z~2.1-4.5. At z~2.2, we observed 13 quasars with Keck/KCWI and targeted the systems with the most prominent extended Lya and HeII emission with Keck/MOSFIRE, providing the first statistical quasar-CGM sample with combined Lya, HeII, and Ha measurements. Within matched apertures out to ~35 pkpc, stacked spectra give Lya/Ha=9.1, HeII/Ha=0.54, and HeII/Lya=0.06. Single-density models require very high CGM densities (n>10 cm^-3) or implausibly soft AGN spectra to reproduce the low HeII/Ha ratio. Broad log-normal density distributions instead reproduce it at lower median densities but require a substantial emissivity-weighted high-density tail, corresponding formally to C~10^3-10^4 in our parameterization. We also analyze 26 VLT/MUSE quasars at 3.1<z<4.5, where Ha is inaccessible from the ground, finding 14 systems with co-spatial extended Lya and HeII emission. The detected, emission-weighted HeII/Lya component shows no evidence for strong evolution between z~2.2 and z~3.7, though this does not imply an invariant underlying density PDF. These constraints provide a basis for comparison with theoretical models and hydrodynamical simulations of the physical processes shaping quasar CGM at high redshift.

AI.tldr: Using CLOUDY photoionization models and Keck/VLT observations, the paper predicts HeII/Ha and HeII/Lya in quasar-illuminated CGM, finding that broad log-normal density distributions with high clumping factors (C~10^3-10^4) are needed to reproduce the low observed HeII/Ha, with no strong HeII/Lya evolution between z~2.2 and z~3.7.
AI.motivation: Extended Lya emission around high-redshift quasars traces large cool CGM reservoirs, but its resonant nature complicates interpretation of gas density, ionization state, and kinematics. Non-resonant tracers like HeII and Ha are essential to break these degeneracies, yet statistical samples combining all three lines were lacking.
AI.method: Extends prior analytical models using CLOUDY photoionization simulations to predict HeII/Ha across a broad parameter range, including log-normal density distributions. Observes 13 quasars at z~2.2 with Keck/KCWI, targeting prominent extended Lya/HeII systems with Keck/MOSFIRE, and analyzes 26 VLT/MUSE quasars at 3.1<z<4.5. Compares models to stacked spectra within ~35 pkpc apertures.
AI.result: Stacked spectra yield Lya/Ha=9.1, HeII/Ha=0.54, and HeII/Lya=0.06. Single-density models require very high CGM densities (n>10 cm^-3) or implausibly soft AGN spectra to reproduce the low HeII/Ha. Broad log-normal density distributions reproduce it at lower median densities but need a substantial emissivity-weighted high-density tail, formally C~10^3-10^4. Among MUSE quasars, 14 show co-spatial extended Lya and HeII; the emission-weighted HeII/Lya shows no strong evolution between z~2.2 and z~3.7.
AI.conclusion: Constraints from combined Lya, HeII, and Ha measurements provide a basis for comparison with theoretical models and hydrodynamical simulations of the physical processes shaping quasar CGM at high redshift. The lack of strong HeII/Lya evolution does not imply an invariant underlying density PDF.

title: Weighing Galaxies Inside-Out: Small-Scale Lensing and the Stellar Mass Problem
comment: 15 pages, 11 figures
summary: Small-scale galaxy-galaxy weak lensing provides an independent way to probe the stellar initial mass function by constraining the matter distribution within galaxies. We forecast the potential of upcoming \textit{Euclid} observations using realistic mock catalogues designed for a DESI-like Bright Galaxy Survey, which is expected to cover approximately $9000\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ of the \textit{Euclid} wide survey area. We assess the impact of foreground lens light, which introduces significant scale-dependent biases in source detection, photometry, and shape measurements. Subtracting the lens light with \textsc{Galfit} reduces these biases by nearly an order of magnitude at scales down to four times the half-light radius. We model the predicted lensing signal around central galaxies with stellar masses between $9.5 \leq \log(M_*/h^{-2}M_\odot) \leq 11.5$ over projected separations of $10$ to $100\,h^{-1}\mathrm{kpc}$. The resulting signal-to-noise ratios reach $\sim 150$ for intermediate-mass galaxies. Assuming an NFW profile for the dark matter contribution, we constrain the stellar mismatch parameter $α$ to a precision of approximately $8.5$ percent for the full sample and $8.6$ percent for massive galaxies. These results highlight the potential of small-scale galaxy--galaxy weak lensing as a robust probe of the IMF and the connection between stellar and dark matter in galaxies using upcoming \textit{Euclid} data.

AI.tldr: Forecast study showing that small-scale galaxy-galaxy weak lensing with Euclid data, using Galfit lens-light subtraction, can constrain the stellar initial mass function via the mismatch parameter α to ~8.5% precision.
AI.motivation: The stellar initial mass function (IMF) can be probed independently through the matter distribution within galaxies via small-scale galaxy-galaxy weak lensing. The authors aim to assess whether upcoming Euclid observations can deliver competitive IMF constraints, while accounting for the dominant systematic of foreground lens light contamination.
AI.method: Realistic mock catalogues were constructed for a DESI-like Bright Galaxy Survey covering ~9000 deg² of the Euclid wide survey. The impact of foreground lens light on source detection, photometry, and shape measurement was quantified, and lens-light subtraction was performed with Galfit. The predicted lensing signal around central galaxies with stellar masses 9.5 ≤ log(M*/h⁻²M⊙) ≤ 11.5 was modeled over projected separations of 10–100 h⁻¹kpc. An NFW profile was assumed for the dark matter contribution, and the stellar mismatch parameter α was constrained.
AI.result: Lens-light subtraction with Galfit reduces scale-dependent biases by nearly an order of magnitude down to scales of four times the half-light radius. Signal-to-noise ratios reach ~150 for intermediate-mass galaxies. The stellar mismatch parameter α is constrained to a precision of ~8.5% for the full sample and ~8.6% for massive galaxies.
AI.conclusion: Small-scale galaxy-galaxy weak lensing is a robust probe of the IMF and of the connection between stellar and dark matter in galaxies, and upcoming Euclid data can deliver ~8.5% precision on α once lens-light systematics are controlled.

title: Galaxy Protoclusters as Drivers of Cosmic Reionization: II. Te-Based Metallicities of Lyman-α Emitters
comment: 9 pages
summary: Context. Protoclusters at reionization are thought to host a significant fraction of the cosmic star formation rate density, making them crucial for the timing and topology of reionization. The gas-phase metallicity, a key tracer of galaxy evolutionary stage, can now be measured directly in the early Universe with JWST. Aims. We measure the gas-phase metallicity of Lyman-$α$ emitters (LAEs) in the LAGER-z7OD1 protocluster at $z\approx6.93$ via the direct ($T_e$-based) method using the [O III]$λ$4363 auroral line, and combine it with stellar masses to constrain the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) in dense environments. Methods. We use JWST/NIRSpec MSA G395H spectroscopy, derive metallicities with self-consistent analytic prescriptions, and propagate the dust-extinction uncertainty into an asymmetric error budget via Monte Carlo simulations based on the observed Balmer decrements. Stellar masses come from BEAGLE SED fitting of JWST/NIRCam and UltraVISTA photometry. Results. We obtain five secure [O III]$λ$4363 detections and one upper limit, with 12+log(O/H) $\approx$ 7.2-8.0. The weighted spectral stack yields 12+log(O/H) = $7.76^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$, ~0.26 dex higher than stacks of LAEs at similar redshifts from JWST surveys. However, the MZR fit gives a slope $γ$ = 0.232 +/- 0.214 and normalization $Z_0$ = 7.888 +/- 0.199, placing our sources below the established MZR of normal galaxies and recent protocluster baselines at $z\sim5-7$. Conclusions. The higher metallicity relative to general LAEs suggests accelerated assembly driven by the overdensity, while the offset below the MZR points to a complex interplay between mass build-up and gas accretion. Since we target actively star-forming LAEs, we are likely capturing a phase of pristine gas inflow from the intergalactic medium that fuels star formation but dilutes the interstellar media of these protocluster members.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec direct-method metallicity measurements of LAEs in the z≈6.93 LAGER-z7OD1 protocluster reveal enhanced metallicity versus field LAEs but a position below the established mass-metallicity relation, suggesting accelerated assembly plus pristine gas inflow.
AI.motivation: Protoclusters at reionization are thought to host a significant fraction of the cosmic star formation rate density, making them crucial for the timing and topology of reionization. Gas-phase metallicity traces galaxy evolutionary stage and is now measurable at high redshift with JWST, motivating a direct-method metallicity census in a dense protocluster environment.
AI.method: JWST/NIRSpec MSA G395H spectroscopy of LAEs in the LAGER-z7OD1 protocluster at z≈6.93; gas-phase metallicities derived via the direct Te method using the [O III]λ4363 auroral line with self-consistent analytic prescriptions; dust-extinction uncertainty propagated into an asymmetric error budget via Monte Carlo simulations based on observed Balmer decrements; stellar masses from BEAGLE SED fitting of JWST/NIRCam and UltraVISTA photometry.
AI.result: Five secure [O III]λ4363 detections and one upper limit, with 12+log(O/H) ≈ 7.2–8.0. The weighted spectral stack gives 12+log(O/H) = 7.76(+0.06/−0.05), ~0.26 dex higher than LAE stacks at similar redshifts from JWST surveys. The MZR fit yields slope γ = 0.232 ± 0.214 and normalization Z0 = 7.888 ± 0.199, placing the sources below the established MZR of normal galaxies and recent protocluster baselines at z ∼ 5–7.
AI.conclusion: The higher metallicity relative to general LAEs suggests accelerated assembly driven by the overdensity, while the offset below the MZR points to a complex interplay between mass build-up and gas accretion. Targeting actively star-forming LAEs likely captures a phase of pristine gas inflow from the intergalactic medium that fuels star formation but dilutes the interstellar media of these protocluster members.

title: Diverse Protoclusters at $z\sim3$ Disclosed by Systematic Spectroscopy
comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We present the results from follow-up spectroscopy of three protocluster candidates at $z\sim3$, selected as overdense regions of $U$-dropout galaxies in the wide-field imaging of the Hyper SuprimeCam Subaru Strategic Programme. All three targets exhibit tight clustering in three-dimensional space, i.e. on the sky ($>4σ$ overdensity) and in redshift ($>98.4\%$ confidence), making for clear evidence of genuine protoclusters. Since these three protoclusters are identified by the same dataset and technique, they represent a good sample to study the diversity of protocluster properties with minimal observational biases. Although the average population across the three protoclusters is consistent with field galaxies, each protocluster individually exhibits distinguishing properties from each other or from field galaxies. In one protocluster, member galaxies stand out by a higher Ly$α$ equivalent width ($EW_0$), and massive members that are still highly star-forming. In contrast, relatively more suppressed star formation appears in another protocluster where the Ly$α$ $EW_0$ of member galaxies is systematically lower. These variations can be attributed to differences in the developmental phase of protoclusters. If the presence of quenching galaxies indicates a more mature system, galaxies with stronger Ly$α$ emissions may be more prevalent in the earlier stages of cluster formation. The uniform approach to searching protoclusters on which this study builds enables us to link observed variations at the onset of cosmic noon to different pathways in the history of cluster formation.

AI.tldr: Follow-up spectroscopy of three z~3 protocluster candidates confirms them as genuine protoclusters and reveals diverse member-galaxy properties attributable to different evolutionary stages.
AI.motivation: Understanding protocluster formation and the diversity of their properties at high redshift requires a homogeneous sample with minimal observational bias, which wide-field imaging alone cannot confirm or characterize.
AI.method: Follow-up spectroscopy of three protocluster candidates at z~3, originally selected as overdense U-dropout regions from Hyper SuprimeCam Subaru Strategic Programme wide-field imaging, to confirm clustering in three-dimensional space and compare member-galaxy properties with field galaxies.
AI.result: All three targets show tight clustering on the sky (>4σ overdensity) and in redshift (>98.4% confidence), confirming them as genuine protoclusters. On average, their member galaxies resemble field galaxies, but individual protoclusters differ: one shows higher Lyα equivalent width (EW0) and massive, highly star-forming members, while another shows systematically lower Lyα EW0 and more suppressed star formation.
AI.conclusion: These variations reflect differences in protocluster developmental phase. Quenching galaxies may indicate a more mature system, whereas stronger Lyα emission may be more common in earlier stages of cluster formation. The uniform search method links observed variations at cosmic noon's onset to different cluster-formation pathways.
